1: # Kallar
2: 
3: ### A multiscript typeface that blooms.
4: 
5: ![Kallar — five scripts, one aperture](proofs/kallar_multiscript.png)
6: 
7: ![License: OFL 1.1](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-OFL%201.1-ee7944)
8: ![Scripts: 5](https://img.shields.io/badge/scripts-5-3d4fbf)
9: ![Variable: APER 0–100](https://img.shields.io/badge/variable-APER%200--100-7f63d6)
10: ![Colour: COLRv1](https://img.shields.io/badge/colour-COLRv1-d973a0)
11: 
12: **Kallar** is a multiscript display type system built around one idea: the
13: counter as a **lotus gateway**. At one end of its variable axis a loop is the
14: classic round form; at the other, its crown rises into a soft petal. The
15: transformation is not a decorative filter — it is a real OpenType variation
16: axis, interpolated from point-compatible outlines.
17: 
18: The family began with Malayalam and now carries the same `APER` axis into
19: **Devanagari (Hindi, Marathi, Nepali), Tamil, Telugu and Kannada**. Each
20: script is a separate variable family because its shaping, glyph set and win
21: metrics are its own; together they share one axis, one set of design stops,
22: one Spectrum palette, Manjari's typographic metrics and one build pipeline.
23: 
24: Every family is built on the **Manjari** skeleton by Santhosh Thottingal and
25: Swathanthra Malayalam Computing. Manjari supplies the shared Latin, digits,
26: punctuation, symbols, spacing, metrics and design language of all five
27: families. Because Manjari is a Malayalam + Latin face, the Devanagari, Tamil,
28: Telugu and Kannada letters use the corresponding **Noto Sans** faces as
29: **script donors**: a donor supplies only the script-specific letter structures
30: and shaping rules, while every shared glyph and the design language come from
31: Manjari. All bases are used under the SIL Open Font License. The aperture
32: engine, variable axis, Spectrum builds, metrics and specimens are new work by
33: the Kallar Project Authors.
34: 
35: Kallar lives at
36: [github.com/kurianbenoy/kallar](https://github.com/kurianbenoy/kallar).

61: ## The idea
62: 
63: Malayalam is a script of loops. The loop head is its most recognisable
64: gesture: a round counter, an opening, a tail. Most typefaces treat that loop
65: as a circle or an oval. Kallar treats it as a **gateway**.
66: 
67: At `APER 0` the counter is a classic round loop. As `APER` rises, the crown of
68: the counter lifts into a soft point: the negative space becomes a lotus petal,
69: a temple doorway. The outer silhouette follows with a gentler version of the
70: same gesture, so open arches and closed loops share one rhythm. The counters
71: themselves change shape — this is outline variation, not a decorative overlay.
72: 
73: The second layer is colour. **Kallar Spectrum** carries a blue → orange
74: gradient inside the font with COLRv1 and CPAL. The gradient is defined once per
75: glyph in font units, so a paragraph reads as one continuous field rather than
76: a set of separately coloured letters.
77: 
78: Kallar is a **display** companion, designed to be set large where the petal
79: crowns and the spectrum are visible. It is also comfortable in short text,
80: where the crowns settle into a quiet, readable rhythm.
81: 
82: ### Design principles
83: 
84: 1. **The counter is the signature.** The transform starts in the negative
85:    space, not on the outer contour.
86: 2. **One grammar, five scripts.** Scripts keep their own shaping and
87:    proportions, but share the same aperture logic.
88: 3. **Point compatibility over effects.** Masters only move existing points, so
89:    every intermediate value is a designed shape and text keeps its metrics.
90: 4. **Colour is part of the type.** The spectrum is painted by the font, not
91:    pasted on top of it.
92: 5. **Honest derivatives.** The base skeleton, the script donors, their authors
93:    and their OFL licences are recorded in the fonts and in this repository.

97: ## Five scripts, one aperture
98: 
99: | Script | Native name | Family | Base | Script donor | Script codepoints | Glyphs |
100: |---|---|---|---|---|---:|---:|
101: | Malayalam | **കല്ലാർ** | `Kallar` | Manjari | — | full block | 918 / 912 |
102: | Devanagari (Hindi) | **कल्लार** | `Kallar Devanagari` | Manjari | Noto Sans Devanagari | 201 | 1151 |
103: | Tamil | **கல்லார்** | `Kallar Tamil` | Manjari | Noto Sans Tamil | 72 | 605 |
104: | Telugu | **కల్లార్** | `Kallar Telugu` | Manjari | Noto Sans Telugu | 100 | 1279 |
105: | Kannada | **ಕಲ್ಲಾರ್** | `Kallar Kannada` | Manjari | Noto Sans Kannada | 91 | 967 |
106: 
107: The **Base** column is the skeleton of every family. The **Script donor**
108: column is only the source of the script-specific letters that Manjari does not
109: contain; it is not the base.
110: 
111: The name **Kallar** is written **കല്ലാർ** in Malayalam, **कल्लार** in
112: Devanagari, **கல்லார்** in Tamil, **కల్లార్** in Telugu and **ಕಲ್ಲಾರ್** in
113: Kannada.
114: 
115: “Hindi” is written in Devanagari; the Devanagari family also covers Marathi,
116: Nepali and Sanskrit. The Tamil, Telugu and Kannada families each cover their
117: own script plus the Latin, digits, punctuation and spacing inherited from
118: Manjari. The Noto Sans files are script donors for the letters Manjari does
119: not contain; they are not the base of the family.
120: 
121: ![The APER axis across four scripts](proofs/kallar_multiscript_axis.png)
122: 
123: ### Script-specific profiles
124: 
125: Each script has its own aperture profile, because the scripts do not share a
126: single counter grammar:
127: 
128: - **Devanagari** keeps the shirorekha dead straight. An absolute freeze at the
129:   headline means only the counters and the loops below it open into petals.
130: - **Tamil** uses a gentler hole-and-crown profile. Its counters are fewer and
131:   more open, so the petal is concentrated in the loops and inner curves.
132: - **Telugu** and **Kannada** take the full hole-and-crown warp. Their round
133:   loops carry the lotus form most naturally.
134: - The warp is restricted to the script's **GSUB closure**, so Latin,
135:   punctuation and unrelated glyphs remain in Manjari's style. The axis changes
136:   the script's counters, never its glyph sequence, spacing or kerning.
137: 
138: The per-script specimens show the full system:

147: ## The APER axis
148: 
149: ![The five stops of the aperture axis](proofs/kallar_axis.png)
150: 
151: Every counter in Kallar can open from a classic round loop (`APER 0`) to a
152: pointed lotus gateway (`APER 100`). The axis has five design stops:
153: 
154: | APER | Name | Character |
155: |---:|---|---|
156: | 0 | Round | The classic loop |
157: | 25 | Quarter | A first lift at the crown |
158: | 50 | Bloom | The gateway begins to open |
159: | 75 | Three-quarters | A clear petal silhouette |
160: | 100 | Petal | The full lotus display cut (default) |
161: 
162: ![The aperture axis in motion](proofs/kallar_aper.gif)
163: 
164: The two masters share the same point topology, so every intermediate value is
165: a designed shape and HarfBuzz shaping is identical at every stop. The axis
166: changes the counters and crowns, never the glyph sequence, the spacing or the
167: kerning.
168: 
169: ```css
170: /* 0 = round · 50 = bloom · 100 = petal */
171: font-variation-settings: "APER" 100;
172: ```

176: ## The Spectrum
177: 
178: ![Kallar Spectrum](proofs/kallar_gradient.png)
179: 
180: **Kallar Spectrum** carries a blue → orange gradient inside the font itself
181: with COLRv1 and CPAL. Blue sits at the crown, orange near the baseline and gold
182: in the descenders, so a paragraph reads as one continuous field rather than a
183: set of separately coloured letters. Regular and Bold Spectrum builds ship for
184: every script.
185: 
186: | Stop | Colour | Role |
187: |---:|---|---|
188: | 0.00 | `#181E5C` | deep indigo |
189: | 0.20 | `#2B3FB0` | blue |
190: | 0.40 | `#5C64DB` | periwinkle |
191: | 0.58 | `#A06CD2` | violet |
192: | 0.74 | `#D973A0` | pink |
193: | 0.88 | `#EE7944` | Sarvam orange |
194: | 1.00 | `#F9C36D` | warm gold |
195: 
196: Clients with COLRv1 support paint the gradient; clients without it fall back
197: to the monochrome outlines. The gradient is clipped to each glyph outline and
198: runs from `y=620` to `y=-120` in font units.
199: 
200: The spectrum is an homage to the lotus-and-gateway visual language of
201: [Sarvam AI](https://www.sarvam.ai/brand). This project is independent and is
202: not affiliated with or endorsed by Sarvam AI.

220: ## Character set
221: 
222: ![Kallar character sheet](proofs/kallar_glyphs.png)
223: 
224: The Malayalam family covers the complete Malayalam block plus Latin:
225: 
226: - 36 consonants, 16 independent vowels, all vowel signs and chillus
227: - Common conjuncts, reph forms, ya/va post-base signs
228: - Malayalam digits ൦–൯ and historical numerals ൰–൵
229: - Rare letters (ഩ ഺ ഽ ൏), chandrabindu, visarga, virama
230: - Latin uppercase/lowercase, digits, punctuation and common accents
231: - **918 glyphs** in Regular, **912** in Bold
232: 
233: The multiscript families retain the full cmap and GSUB coverage of their
234: script donors: Devanagari includes the Devanagari block, Devanagari Extended
235: and the Vedic extensions supported by the donor; Tamil, Telugu and Kannada
236: include their full blocks. The shared Latin, digits, punctuation and symbols
237: are Manjari's. Coverage and the Manjari base are verified in
238: `tests/test_multiscript.py`.

309: ## Using Kallar
310: 
311: ### Web
312: 
313: ```css
314: @font-face {
315:   font-family: "Kallar";
316:   src: url("Kallar-Regular.woff2") format("woff2");
317:   font-weight: 400;
318:   font-display: swap;
319: }
320: 
321: @font-face {
322:   font-family: "Kallar";
323:   src: url("Kallar-Bold.woff2") format("woff2");
324:   font-weight: 700;
325:   font-display: swap;
326: }
327: 
328: .bloom {
329:   font-family: "Kallar";
330:   font-weight: 700;
331:   font-variation-settings: "APER" 100; /* 0 = round, 100 = petal */
332: }
333: ```
334: 
335: ### Devanagari, Tamil, Telugu and Kannada
336: 
337: ```css
338: @font-face {
339:   font-family: "Kallar Devanagari";
340:   src: url("KallarDevanagari-Regular.woff2") format("woff2");
341:   font-weight: 400;
342: }
343: 
344: .deva {
345:   font-family: "Kallar Devanagari";
346:   font-variation-settings: "APER" 100;
347: }
348: ```
349: 
350: ### Mixed-script copy
351: 
352: Stack the families. The browser picks the first family that supports each
353: character — the Malayalam family handles Malayalam and the shared Latin, and
354: the script families fill in the rest:
355: 
356: ```css
357: .multiscript {
358:   font-family:
359:     "Kallar",
360:     "Kallar Devanagari",
361:     "Kallar Tamil",
362:     "Kallar Telugu",
363:     "Kallar Kannada",
364:     sans-serif;
365:   font-variation-settings: "APER" 100;
366: }
367: ```
368: 
369: ### Colour
370: 
371: Use `Kallar-SpectrumRegular` / `Kallar-Spectrum`, or the corresponding
372: `Kallar<Script>-Spectrum*` builds. Clients with COLRv1 support paint the
373: gradient; clients without it fall back to the monochrome outlines.
374: 
375: ```css
376: .spectrum {
377:   font-family: "Kallar Spectrum", "Kallar", sans-serif;
378:   font-weight: 700;
379: }
380: ```
381: 
382: ### JavaScript
383: 
384: ```js
385: const title = document.querySelector(".bloom");
386: title.style.fontVariationSettings = '"APER" 65';
387: ```
388: 
389: ### HarfBuzz
390: 
391: ```python
392: import uharfbuzz as hb
393: 
394: blob = hb.Blob.from_file_path("KallarDevanagari-Regular.ttf")
395: face = hb.Face(blob)
396: font = hb.Font(face)
397: font.set_variations({"APER": 65})
398: ```
399: 
400: ### The APER value
401: 
402: | Value | Use it for |
403: |---:|---|
404: | 0 | A conventional, round text cut |
405: | 25–50 | A subtle display lift |
406: | 50–75 | A clear petal silhouette |
407: | 100 | The full lotus display cut (default) |

411: ## Building from source
412: 
413: The build is Python + fontTools + varLib + COLRv1.
414: 
415: ```bash
416: make venv            # create .venv and install dependencies
417: make kallar          # Malayalam: masters, variable fonts, Spectrum, instances
418: make multiscript     # Devanagari, Tamil, Telugu and Kannada families
419: make test            # shaping, variation and colour tests for all five scripts
420: make proofs          # specimen PNGs, GIF and both interactive HTML specimens
421: make pdf             # Malayalam vector PDF specimen

1: # Kallar
2: 
3: ### A multiscript typeface that blooms.
4: 
5: ![Kallar — five scripts, one aperture](proofs/kallar_multiscript.png)
6: 
7: ![License: OFL 1.1](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-OFL%201.1-ee7944)
8: ![Scripts: 5](https://img.shields.io/badge/scripts-5-3d4fbf)
9: ![Variable: APER 0–100](https://img.shields.io/badge/variable-APER%200--100-7f63d6)
10: ![Colour: COLRv1](https://img.shields.io/badge/colour-COLRv1-d973a0)
11: 
12: **Kallar** is a multiscript display type system built around one idea: the
13: counter as a **lotus gateway**. At one end of its variable axis a loop is the
14: classic round form; at the other, its crown rises into a soft petal. The
15: transformation is not a decorative filter — it is a real OpenType variation
16: axis, interpolated from point-compatible outlines.
17: 
18: The family began with Malayalam and now carries the same `APER` axis into
19: **Devanagari (Hindi, Marathi, Nepali), Tamil, Telugu and Kannada**. Each
20: script is a separate variable family because its shaping, glyph set and win
21: metrics are its own; together they share one axis, one set of design stops,
22: one Spectrum palette, Manjari's typographic metrics and one build pipeline.
23: 
24: Every family is built on the **Manjari** skeleton by Santhosh Thottingal and
25: Swathanthra Malayalam Computing. Manjari supplies the shared Latin, digits,
26: punctuation, symbols, spacing, metrics and design language of all five
27: families. Because Manjari is a Malayalam + Latin face, the Devanagari, Tamil,
28: Telugu and Kannada letters use the corresponding **Noto Sans** faces as
29: **script donors**: a donor supplies only the script-specific letter structures
30: and shaping rules, while every shared glyph and the design language come from
31: Manjari. All bases are used under the SIL Open Font License. The aperture
32: engine, variable axis, Spectrum builds, metrics and specimens are new work by
33: the Kallar Project Authors.
34: 
35: Kallar lives at
36: [github.com/kurianbenoy/kallar](https://github.com/kurianbenoy/kallar).
37: 
38: ---
39: 
40: ## Contents
41: 
42: - [The idea](#the-idea)
43: - [Five scripts, one aperture](#five-scripts-one-aperture)
44: - [The APER axis](#the-aper-axis)

59: ---
60: 
61: ## The idea
62: 
63: Malayalam is a script of loops. The loop head is its most recognisable
64: gesture: a round counter, an opening, a tail. Most typefaces treat that loop
65: as a circle or an oval. Kallar treats it as a **gateway**.
66: 
67: At `APER 0` the counter is a classic round loop. As `APER` rises, the crown of
68: the counter lifts into a soft point: the negative space becomes a lotus petal,
69: a temple doorway. The outer silhouette follows with a gentler version of the
70: same gesture, so open arches and closed loops share one rhythm. The counters
71: themselves change shape — this is outline variation, not a decorative overlay.
72: 
73: The second layer is colour. **Kallar Spectrum** carries a blue → orange
74: gradient inside the font with COLRv1 and CPAL. The gradient is defined once per
75: glyph in font units, so a paragraph reads as one continuous field rather than
76: a set of separately coloured letters.
77: 
78: Kallar is a **display** companion, designed to be set large where the petal
79: crowns and the spectrum are visible. It is also comfortable in short text,
80: where the crowns settle into a quiet, readable rhythm.
81: 
82: ### Design principles
83: 
84: 1. **The counter is the signature.** The transform starts in the negative
85:    space, not on the outer contour.
86: 2. **One grammar, five scripts.** Scripts keep their own shaping and
87:    proportions, but share the same aperture logic.
88: 3. **Point compatibility over effects.** Masters only move existing points, so
89:    every intermediate value is a designed shape and text keeps its metrics.
90: 4. **Colour is part of the type.** The spectrum is painted by the font, not
91:    pasted on top of it.
92: 5. **Honest derivatives.** The base skeleton, the script donors, their authors
93:    and their OFL licences are recorded in the fonts and in this repository.
94: 
95: ---
96: 
97: ## Five scripts, one aperture
98: 
99: | Script | Native name | Family | Base | Script donor | Script codepoints | Glyphs |
100: |---|---|---|---|---|---:|---:|
101: | Malayalam | **കല്ലാർ** | `Kallar` | Manjari | — | full block | 918 / 912 |
102: | Devanagari (Hindi) | **कल्लार** | `Kallar Devanagari` | Manjari | Noto Sans Devanagari | 201 | 1151 |
103: | Tamil | **கல்லார்** | `Kallar Tamil` | Manjari | Noto Sans Tamil | 72 | 605 |
104: | Telugu | **కల్లార్** | `Kallar Telugu` | Manjari | Noto Sans Telugu | 100 | 1279 |
105: | Kannada | **ಕಲ್ಲಾರ್** | `Kallar Kannada` | Manjari | Noto Sans Kannada | 91 | 967 |
106: 
107: The **Base** column is the skeleton of every family. The **Script donor**
108: column is only the source of the script-specific letters that Manjari does not
109: contain; it is not the base.
110: 
111: The name **Kallar** is written **കല്ലാർ** in Malayalam, **कल्लार** in
112: Devanagari, **கல்லார்** in Tamil, **కల్లార్** in Telugu and **ಕಲ್ಲಾರ್** in
113: Kannada.
114: 
115: “Hindi” is written in Devanagari; the Devanagari family also covers Marathi,
116: Nepali and Sanskrit. The Tamil, Telugu and Kannada families each cover their
117: own script plus the Latin, digits, punctuation and spacing inherited from
118: Manjari. The Noto Sans files are script donors for the letters Manjari does
119: not contain; they are not the base of the family.
120: 
121: ![The APER axis across four scripts](proofs/kallar_multiscript_axis.png)
122: 
123: ### Script-specific profiles
124: 
125: Each script has its own aperture profile, because the scripts do not share a
126: single counter grammar:
127: 
128: - **Devanagari** keeps the shirorekha dead straight. An absolute freeze at the
129:   headline means only the counters and the loops below it open into petals.
130: - **Tamil** uses a gentler hole-and-crown profile. Its counters are fewer and
131:   more open, so the petal is concentrated in the loops and inner curves.
132: - **Telugu** and **Kannada** take the full hole-and-crown warp. Their round
133:   loops carry the lotus form most naturally.
134: - The warp is restricted to the script's **GSUB closure**, so Latin,
135:   punctuation and unrelated glyphs remain in Manjari's style. The axis changes
136:   the script's counters, never its glyph sequence, spacing or kerning.
137: 
138: The per-script specimens show the full system:
139: 
140: | | |
141: |---|---|
142: | ![Devanagari](proofs/kallar_devanagari.png) | ![Tamil](proofs/kallar_tamil.png) |
143: | ![Telugu](proofs/kallar_telugu.png) | ![Kannada](proofs/kallar_kannada.png) |
144: 
145: ---
146: 
147: ## The APER axis
148: 
149: ![The five stops of the aperture axis](proofs/kallar_axis.png)
150: 
151: Every counter in Kallar can open from a classic round loop (`APER 0`) to a
152: pointed lotus gateway (`APER 100`). The axis has five design stops:
153: 
154: | APER | Name | Character |
155: |---:|---|---|
156: | 0 | Round | The classic loop |
157: | 25 | Quarter | A first lift at the crown |
158: | 50 | Bloom | The gateway begins to open |
159: | 75 | Three-quarters | A clear petal silhouette |
160: | 100 | Petal | The full lotus display cut (default) |
161: 
162: ![The aperture axis in motion](proofs/kallar_aper.gif)
163: 
164: The two masters share the same point topology, so every intermediate value is
165: a designed shape and HarfBuzz shaping is identical at every stop. The axis
166: changes the counters and crowns, never the glyph sequence, the spacing or the
167: kerning.
168: 
169: ```css
170: /* 0 = round · 50 = bloom · 100 = petal */
171: font-variation-settings: "APER" 100;
172: ```
173: 
174: ---
175: 
176: ## The Spectrum
177: 
178: ![Kallar Spectrum](proofs/kallar_gradient.png)
179: 
180: **Kallar Spectrum** carries a blue → orange gradient inside the font itself
181: with COLRv1 and CPAL. Blue sits at the crown, orange near the baseline and gold
182: in the descenders, so a paragraph reads as one continuous field rather than a
183: set of separately coloured letters. Regular and Bold Spectrum builds ship for
184: every script.
185: 
186: | Stop | Colour | Role |
187: |---:|---|---|
188: | 0.00 | `#181E5C` | deep indigo |
189: | 0.20 | `#2B3FB0` | blue |
190: | 0.40 | `#5C64DB` | periwinkle |
191: | 0.58 | `#A06CD2` | violet |
192: | 0.74 | `#D973A0` | pink |
193: | 0.88 | `#EE7944` | Sarvam orange |
194: | 1.00 | `#F9C36D` | warm gold |
195: 
196: Clients with COLRv1 support paint the gradient; clients without it fall back
197: to the monochrome outlines. The gradient is clipped to each glyph outline and
198: runs from `y=620` to `y=-120` in font units.
199: 
200: The spectrum is an homage to the lotus-and-gateway visual language of
201: [Sarvam AI](https://www.sarvam.ai/brand). This project is independent and is
202: not affiliated with or endorsed by Sarvam AI.
203: 
204: ---

206: ## In context
207: 
208: The same fonts, the same axis, the same spectrum — applied to the kinds of
209: surfaces a contemporary Indian type system has to live on.

218: ---
219: 
220: ## Character set
221: 
222: ![Kallar character sheet](proofs/kallar_glyphs.png)
223: 
224: The Malayalam family covers the complete Malayalam block plus Latin:
225: 
226: - 36 consonants, 16 independent vowels, all vowel signs and chillus
227: - Common conjuncts, reph forms, ya/va post-base signs
228: - Malayalam digits ൦–൯ and historical numerals ൰–൵
229: - Rare letters (ഩ ഺ ഽ ൏), chandrabindu, visarga, virama
230: - Latin uppercase/lowercase, digits, punctuation and common accents
231: - **918 glyphs** in Regular, **912** in Bold
232: 
233: The multiscript families retain the full cmap and GSUB coverage of their
234: script donors: Devanagari includes the Devanagari block, Devanagari Extended
235: and the Vedic extensions supported by the donor; Tamil, Telugu and Kannada
236: include their full blocks. The shared Latin, digits, punctuation and symbols
237: are Manjari's. Coverage and the Manjari base are verified in
238: `tests/test_multiscript.py`.
239: 
240: | Family | Script cmap | Colour glyphs (Spectrum) |
241: |---|---:|---:|
242: | Kallar (Malayalam) | full block | 913 Regular / 907 Bold |
243: | Kallar Devanagari | 201 | 1144 |
244: | Kallar Tamil | 72 | 598 |
245: | Kallar Telugu | 100 | 1273 |
246: | Kallar Kannada | 91 | 961 |
247: 
248: ---
249: 
250: ## The family
251: 
252: Each of the five script families ships the same seven styles. All files are
253: available as TTF and WOFF2.
254: 
255: ### Malayalam
256: 
257: | File | What it is |
258: |---|---|
259: | `fonts/Kallar-Regular.ttf/.woff2` | Variable Regular, `APER` 0–100 (default 100) |
260: | `fonts/Kallar-Bold.ttf/.woff2` | Variable Bold, `APER` 0–100 (default 100) |
261: | `fonts/Kallar-Spectrum.ttf/.woff2` | Variable Bold + COLRv1 spectrum |
262: | `fonts/Kallar-SpectrumRegular.ttf/.woff2` | Variable Regular + COLRv1 spectrum |
263: | `fonts/Kallar-Round.ttf/.woff2` | Static `APER 0` instance |
264: | `fonts/Kallar-Petal.ttf/.woff2` | Static `APER 100` instance |
265: | `fonts/Kallar-BoldPetal.ttf/.woff2` | Static Bold `APER 100` instance |
266: 
267: ### Multiscript
268: 
269: | Family | Files |
270: |---|---|
271: | Kallar Devanagari | `fonts/KallarDevanagari-{Regular,Bold,Round,Petal,BoldPetal,Spectrum,SpectrumRegular}.{ttf,woff2}` |
272: | Kallar Tamil | `fonts/KallarTamil-{Regular,Bold,Round,Petal,BoldPetal,Spectrum,SpectrumRegular}.{ttf,woff2}` |
273: | Kallar Telugu | `fonts/KallarTelugu-{Regular,Bold,Round,Petal,BoldPetal,Spectrum,SpectrumRegular}.{ttf,woff2}` |
274: | Kallar Kannada | `fonts/KallarKannada-{Regular,Bold,Round,Petal,BoldPetal,Spectrum,SpectrumRegular}.{ttf,woff2}` |
275: 
276: ### Specimens
277: 
278: | File | What it is |
279: |---|---|
280: | `specimen/index.html` | Interactive Malayalam specimen (fonts embedded) |
281: | `specimen/multiscript.html` | Interactive five-script specimen with a shared APER slider |
282: | `proofs/Kallar-Specimen.pdf` | Vector Malayalam PDF specimen |
283: | `proofs/Kallar-Multiscript-Specimen.pdf` | Vector multiscript PDF specimen |
284: 
285: ---
286: 
287: ## Download
288: 
289: The latest TTF and WOFF2 builds live in [`fonts/`](fonts/). The multiscript
290: specimen is [`specimen/multiscript.html`](specimen/multiscript.html); the
291: vector PDF is
292: [`proofs/Kallar-Multiscript-Specimen.pdf`](proofs/Kallar-Multiscript-Specimen.pdf).
293: Open the HTML directly, or serve both specimens with:
294: 
295: ```bash
296: make serve   # http://localhost:8000
297: ```
298: 
299: For most web projects, use the WOFF2 variable fonts. For desktop design apps,
300: install the TTF variable fonts. If an app does not expose custom variation
301: axes, use the static `Round` (APER 0) or `Petal` (APER 100) instances.
302: 
303: > **Note:** the five script families are deliberately separate fonts. There is
304: > no single merged all-script TTF, because each script has its own GSUB/GPOS
305: > tables, glyph names and win metrics.
306: 
307: ---
308: 
309: ## Using Kallar
310: 
311: ### Web
312: 
313: ```css
314: @font-face {
315:   font-family: "Kallar";
316:   src: url("Kallar-Regular.woff2") format("woff2");
317:   font-weight: 400;
318:   font-display: swap;
319: }
320: 
321: @font-face {
322:   font-family: "Kallar";
323:   src: url("Kallar-Bold.woff2") format("woff2");
324:   font-weight: 700;
325:   font-display: swap;
326: }
327: 
328: .bloom {
329:   font-family: "Kallar";
330:   font-weight: 700;
331:   font-variation-settings: "APER" 100; /* 0 = round, 100 = petal */
332: }
333: ```
334: 
335: ### Devanagari, Tamil, Telugu and Kannada
336: 
337: ```css
338: @font-face {
339:   font-family: "Kallar Devanagari";
340:   src: url("KallarDevanagari-Regular.woff2") format("woff2");
341:   font-weight: 400;
342: }
343: 
344: .deva {
345:   font-family: "Kallar Devanagari";
346:   font-variation-settings: "APER" 100;
347: }
348: ```
349: 
350: ### Mixed-script copy
351: 
352: Stack the families. The browser picks the first family that supports each
353: character — the Malayalam family handles Malayalam and the shared Latin, and
354: the script families fill in the rest:
355: 
356: ```css
357: .multiscript {
358:   font-family:
359:     "Kallar",
360:     "Kallar Devanagari",
361:     "Kallar Tamil",
362:     "Kallar Telugu",
363:     "Kallar Kannada",
364:     sans-serif;
365:   font-variation-settings: "APER" 100;
366: }
367: ```
368: 
369: ### Colour
370: 
371: Use `Kallar-SpectrumRegular` / `Kallar-Spectrum`, or the corresponding
372: `Kallar<Script>-Spectrum*` builds. Clients with COLRv1 support paint the
373: gradient; clients without it fall back to the monochrome outlines.
374: 
375: ```css
376: .spectrum {
377:   font-family: "Kallar Spectrum", "Kallar", sans-serif;
378:   font-weight: 700;
379: }
380: ```
381: 
382: ### JavaScript
383: 
384: ```js
385: const title = document.querySelector(".bloom");
386: title.style.fontVariationSettings = '"APER" 65';
387: ```
388: 
389: ### HarfBuzz
390: 
391: ```python
392: import uharfbuzz as hb
393: 
394: blob = hb.Blob.from_file_path("KallarDevanagari-Regular.ttf")
395: face = hb.Face(blob)
396: font = hb.Font(face)
397: font.set_variations({"APER": 65})
398: ```
399: 
400: ### The APER value
401: 
402: | Value | Use it for |
403: |---:|---|
404: | 0 | A conventional, round text cut |
405: | 25–50 | A subtle display lift |
406: | 50–75 | A clear petal silhouette |
407: | 100 | The full lotus display cut (default) |
408: 
409: ---
410: 
411: ## Building from source
412: 
413: The build is Python + fontTools + varLib + COLRv1.
414: 
415: ```bash
416: make venv            # create .venv and install dependencies
417: make kallar          # Malayalam: masters, variable fonts, Spectrum, instances
418: make multiscript     # Devanagari, Tamil, Telugu and Kannada families
419: make test            # shaping, variation and colour tests for all five scripts
420: make proofs          # specimen PNGs, GIF and both interactive HTML specimens
421: make pdf             # Malayalam vector PDF specimen
422: make pdf-multiscript # multiscript vector PDF specimen
423: make qa              # fontbakery on Malayalam Regular and Bold
424: make qa-multiscript  # fontbakery on the four new Regular/Bold families
425: ```
426: 
427: `make kamalam` remains as a deprecated alias for the old v1.000 target name.
428: 
429: ### Source layout
430: 
431: | Path | What it is |
432: |---|---|
433: | `tools/kallar.py` | The aperture engine, Malayalam build, spectrum, instances |
434: | `tools/multiscript.py` | The Manjari-base Devanagari/Tamil/Telugu/Kannada build driver |
435: | `tools/specimen.py` | Malayalam proof images and brand mockups |
436: | `tools/specimen_multiscript.py` | Multiscript hero, axis and script sheets |
437: | `tools/specimen_html.py` | Self-contained Malayalam HTML specimen |
438: | `tools/specimen_multiscript_html.py` | Self-contained multiscript HTML specimen |
439: | `tools/pdf.py` | Chromium PDF printer |
440: | `sources/base/` | Manjari base fonts + upstream OFL text |
441: | `sources/donors/` | Noto Sans script donors + upstream OFL texts |
442: | `tests/test_kallar.py` | Malayalam shaping, variation and colour tests |
443: | `tests/test_multiscript.py` | Multiscript axes, Manjari base, metadata, coverage and colour tests |
444: 
445: ### Reproducible builds
446: 
447: `head.created` and `head.modified` are pinned to a fixed date and
448: `recalcTimestamp` is disabled. Repeated `make kallar` and `make multiscript`
449: runs produce byte-identical TTF and WOFF2 files. `make proofs` is
450: deterministic too.
451: 
452: ---
453: 
454: ## Testing and QA
455: 
456: - HarfBuzz shaping across `APER 0`, `50` and `100` for every script — identical
457:   glyph sequences and advances, no `.notdef` in any test case.
458: - Full cmap coverage of each script donor, plus conjuncts, matras, reph forms
459:   and the Devanagari Vedic extensions supported by the donor.
460: - The shared Latin, digits, punctuation and spacing are byte-for-byte
461:   Manjari's outlines and advances in every family, and the Latin kern pairs
462:   use Manjari's lookups.
463: - Outline variation at the two extremes, and a guard that Latin stays
464:   untouched in the script families.
465: - Static Round/Petal instances differ from each other and carry the correct
466:   names; COLRv1/CPAL paint graphs are present in every Spectrum build.
467: - Fontbakery universal: **0 FAIL** on all eight multiscript Regular/Bold
468:   variable fonts. The same documented custom-axis and Bold/`fsSelection`
469:   exclusions as Malayalam are used, plus numeric STAT labels that stay inside
470:   the Windows 31-character limit. Inherited donor warnings are listed in
471:   [NOTES.md](NOTES.md).
472: - Both HTML specimens and the COLRv1 gradient were verified in headless
473:   Chromium 156; the shared APER slider drives all four script families.
474: - Byte-identical repeat builds for `make kallar` and `make multiscript`.
475: 
476: ---
477: 
478: ## Design notes
479: 
480: The full design and engineering rationale is in [NOTES.md](NOTES.md),
481: including:
482: 
483: - why Manjari is the base of every family;
484: - what the Noto Sans script donors contribute and why;
485: - the exact aperture parameters for each script;
486: - why Devanagari needs an absolute headline freeze;
487: - how the GSUB closure keeps Latin in Manjari's style;
488: - metrics, reproducibility, fontbakery exclusions and known limits.
489: 
490: The short version:
491: 
492: | Script | Profile |
493: |---|---|
494: | Malayalam | Full hole-and-crown warp; the original Kallar cut |
495: | Devanagari | Counters-only below an absolute headline freeze |
496: | Tamil | Gentler profile concentrated in the fewer closed loops |
497: | Telugu | Full hole-and-crown warp |
498: | Kannada | Full hole-and-crown warp |

6: digits, punctuation, symbols, spacing, metrics and design language. The
7: Devanagari, Tamil, Telugu and Kannada branches use the corresponding Noto Sans
8: faces only as script donors, because Manjari has no glyphs for those scripts.

10: COLRv1 blue→orange Spectrum builds.

15:   shared Latin, digits, punctuation, symbols, spacing, metrics, x-height,
16:   cap-height and Latin kerning of every family.

18:   script donors for the script-specific letter structures Manjari does not

24:   sized to each script's outline extents. OS/2 x-height and cap-height now
25:   follow Manjari.

1: # Kallar — design & engineering notes
2: 
3: ## 1. The idea
4: 
5: Malayalam is a loop script. The loop head (തല) is the script's most recognisable
6: gesture: a round counter, an opening, a tail. Most Malayalam typefaces treat
7: that loop as a circle or an oval. Kallar treats it as a **gateway**.
8: 
9: At `APER 0` the counter is the classic round loop inherited from Manjari. As
10: `APER` rises, the crown of the counter lifts into a soft point: the negative
11: space becomes a lotus petal / a temple doorway. The outer silhouette follows
12: with a gentler version of the same gesture, so open arches (മ, ന, ത) and closed
13: loops (ക, ഖ, ങ) share one rhythm. The result is not a decorative overlay; the
14: *counters themselves* change shape.
15: 
16: The second layer is colour. Sarvam's identity uses a blue → orange spectrum and
17: a lotus/gateway monogram. Kallar Spectrum carries a vertical
18: blue → orange gradient inside the font with COLRv1, clipped to each glyph. At
19: text sizes the tops are blue, the baseline zone is pink/orange and the
20: descenders are gold — one continuous field across the text block.
21: 
22: The family is deliberately a **display** companion, not a replacement for a
23: text face. It is designed to be set large, where the petal crowns and the
24: spectrum are visible.
25: 
26: ## 2. Why Manjari is the skeleton
27: 
28: The project's first two versions attempted a fully from-scratch parametric
29: Malayalam design (`legacy/`, `tools/glyphs_ml.py`). That work proved the
30: pipeline and the shaping stack, but matching the structural subtlety of a
31: production Malayalam face — the exact placement of loops, the counter rhythm,
32: the conjunct grammar — is a years-long project. For the production release we
33: made a deliberate choice:
34: 
35: - use **Manjari** (SIL OFL 1.1, by Santhosh Thottingal / SMC) as the
36:   structural foundation, because its loops and proportions are already a
37:   high-quality expression of the script;
38: - keep the base unmodified in `sources/base/` and record the transformation in
39:   code;
40: - do the new work where it is genuinely new: the aperture engine, the variable
41:   axis, the colour build, the metrics and the specimen.
42: 
43: This is a common and legitimate model in type design: a new face can share a
44: skeleton with an established one while having a distinct design language. The
45: derived font is renamed, the original copyright is preserved in the name table,
46: and the build is reproducible. The OFL permits this; the attribution is in the
47: font metadata, the README, the specimen and `AUTHORS.md`.
48: 
49: ## 3. The aperture transform
50: 
51: ### 3.1 Point compatibility
52: 
53: `varLib` requires masters with identical point topology. The transform
54: therefore only **moves existing TrueType points**; it never adds or removes
55: contours or points. Both the round master and the petal master start from the
56: same scaled Manjari source:
57: 
58: ```
59: Manjari-Regular.ttf (2048 UPM)
60:   └─ scale_upem → 1000 UPM
61:        ├─ round master: no warp
62:        └─ petal master: petal_warp()
63: ```
64: 
65: Because the point count, contour order and glyph order are unchanged, the
66: `gvar` deltas are exact and interpolation is smooth at every intermediate
67: value.
68: 
69: ### 3.2 Counter crowns
70: 
71: For each hole contour:
72: 
73: 1. compute its bbox and centre;
74: 2. for each point in the upper 55% of the hole, compute `u = (x-cx)/rx`,
75:    `v = (y-ymin)/h`, `t = (v-0.45)/0.55`;
76: 3. find the nearest outer-contour point with a KD-tree;
77: 4. lift the point by
78:    `bump * (1-u²) * t²`, where `bump = min(hole_bump, cap_frac * distance)`;
79: 5. pinch it horizontally by `pin * u * t²` to sharpen the crown.
80: 
81: The distance cap is essential. Manjari's strokes are ~65 units at 1000 UPM; an
82: uncapped 110-unit lift would push the counter through the outer contour and
83: create a hairline notch. Capping at 55% of the nearest stroke thickness makes
84: the petal safe on every glyph, including the tiny loops of ഇ, ഈ, ഠ and the
85: historical numerals. The cap varies per point, so the warp stays smooth.
86: 
87: ### 3.3 Outer crowns
88: 
89: Open counters (മ, ന, ത, യ, …) are not holes; their inner edge is part of the
90: outer contour. To bring them into the same language, the engine finds local
91: maxima on every outer contour in the upper half of the glyph and applies a
92: smooth Gaussian lift:
93: 
94: ```
95: wy = clamp((y - (gymin+0.35*gh)) / (0.65*gh), 0, 1)
96: pull = exp(-((x-px)/sigma)^2) * wy^2
97: y += peak_bump * pull
98: x -= 0.5 * pinch * (x-px) * exp(...) * wy
99: ```
100: 
101: `sigma` is relative to the contour width, so wide letters get a broad crown and
102: narrow letters a tighter one. The lift is subtle enough that the counters stay
103: open and readable.
104: 
105: ### 3.4 Parameters at 1000 UPM
106: 
107: | parameter | value | role |
108: |---|---:|---|
109: | `hole_bump` | 110 | maximum counter crown lift |
110: | `peak_bump` | 40 | outer crown lift |
111: | `sigma_f` | 0.28 | crown width relative to contour width |
112: | `pinch` | 0.055 | horizontal sharpening |
113: | `cap_frac` | 0.55 | maximum lift as a fraction of local stroke |
114: 
115: The static `APER 0`, `50`, `100` instances are produced with
116: `fontTools.varLib.instancer`.
117: 
118: ## 4. Metrics
119: 
120: The base is scaled to 1000 UPM. The final metrics are:
121: 
122: - `sTypoAscender = 800`, `sTypoDescender = -300`, `sTypoLineGap = 0`
123: - `hhea.ascent = 800`, `hhea.descent = -300`, `lineGap = 0`
124: - `usWinAscent = 1100`, `usWinDescent = 700` (the real glyph extents are
125:   roughly -614…1075, so the win metrics never clip)
126: - `USE_TYPO_METRICS` (OS/2 fsSelection bit 7) is set.
127: - The vertical metrics are intentionally generous: Malayalam marks, chillus
128:   and the Latin superscripts extend above the nominal ascender.
129: 
130: Manjari's advances, kerning and GSUB/GPOS are preserved. The warp only changes
131: outline coordinates, so spacing and shaping stay stable across the axis.
132: 
133: ## 5. COLRv1 spectrum
134: 
135: The Spectrum builds start from the variable Regular and Bold and add:
136: 
137: - `CPAL` with a 7-entry palette:
138:   `#181E5C`, `#2B3FB0`, `#5C64DB`, `#A06CD2`, `#D973A0`, `#EE7944`, `#F9C36D`.
139: - `COLR` version 1 with one `BaseGlyphPaintRecord` per non-empty glyph:
140:   `PaintGlyph(glyph)` → `PaintLinearGradient`.
141: - The gradient runs from `(0, 620)` to `(0, -120)`, with the rotation point
142:   `(500, 620)` (perpendicular to the gradient direction). The gradient is in
143:   font units and is clipped by the glyph outline. This range puts blue at the
144:   top of the body, orange near the baseline and gold in the descenders.
145: - 907 glyphs carry a paint record in the Bold build and 913 in the Regular
146:   build; the rest fall back to monochrome.
147: 
148: Browsers/apps with COLRv1 (Chrome, Edge, Figma, recent Safari) paint the
149: gradient; apps without it render the base outlines. The specimen also shows a
150: CSS gradient-clipped version so the visual idea is visible everywhere.
151: 
152: ## 6. Testing
153: 
154: `tests/test_kallar.py` checks:
155: 
156: - `fvar` axis `APER = 0…100`, default 100;
157: - `STAT` axis values Round / Bloom / Petal;
158: - the OFL name table and Manjari attribution on every build;
159: - shaping of 35+ Malayalam strings at `APER 0`, `50`, `100`, with identical
160:   glyph sequences;
161: - coverage of every assigned Malayalam codepoint;
162: - outline variation between the extremes;
163: - COLR/CPAL structure, 907 paint records and 7 palette entries.
164: 
165: The HTML specimen was also checked in headless Chromium 156: the embedded
166: variable fonts load, the APER slider changes the live instance, and the
167: `Kallar Spectrum` sample paints its COLRv1 gradient in the browser.
168: 
169: Builds are reproducible: `head.created`/`head.modified` are pinned to a fixed
170: date and `recalcTimestamp` is disabled, so repeated `make kallar` runs produce
171: byte-identical TTF and WOFF2 files. `make proofs` is deterministic too.
172: 
173: The old `tests/test_font.py` still covers the legacy draft.
174: 
175: ## 7. Fontbakery notes
176: 
177: The Regular font passes `fontbakery check-universal` with two exclusions that
178: do not apply to this design:
179: 
180: - `opentype/fvar/regular_coords_correct` assumes a registered `wght`/`wdth`
181:   axis; Kallar's only axis is the custom `APER`.
182: - `alt_caron` is a Czech/Slovak-specific check that wants `ď` to use a
183:   non-standard caron glyph. The Latin `ď` here uses a combining caron, which
184:   is typographically correct; the check is not relevant to a Malayalam face.
185: 
186: For the Bold and Spectrum builds, `opentype/fsselection` and
187: `opentype/mac_style` also need excluding because fontbakery infers "Bold"
188: from a `wght` axis or a filename convention and cannot see the custom-axis
189: Bold style; the OS/2 and `head` values themselves are correct. Run the QA
190: target with:
191: 
192: ```bash
193: make qa
194: ```
195: 
196: The specimen HTML and COLRv1 paint were verified in headless Chromium 156.
197: 
198: ## 8. Known limits / next work
199: 
200: - The transform is derived from Manjari's skeleton; it is not a new
201:   construction from a blank page. A future release could redraw the skeleton
202:   from the same aperture grammar while keeping the axis.
203: - The Spectrum gradient is static; a `COLRv1` variable gradient tied to `APER`
204:   would be the next step.
205: - A `wght` axis would need point-compatible masters from a variable source
206:   (Noto Sans Malayalam is a candidate) or a carefully offset master.
207: - The display cut is optimised for large sizes. A text-optimised cut with
208:   smaller petal lifts and looser spacing is planned.
209: 
210: ## 9. The multiscript extension
211: 
212: ### 9.1 Manjari is the base of every family
213: 
214: The original idea is preserved: all five Kallar families start from the
215: **Manjari** skeleton. Manjari supplies the shared Latin, digits, punctuation,
216: symbols, spacing, metrics and design language. The Malayalam family is Manjari
217: throughout.
218: 
219: Manjari is a Malayalam + Latin face, so it has no Devanagari, Tamil, Telugu or
220: Kannada glyphs. Drawing four new scripts from a blank page would be a
221: years-long design project, and a from-scratch skeleton would not have Manjari's
222: quality. The release therefore uses one OFL **script donor** per
223: non-Malayalam script. The donor supplies only the script-specific letter
224: structures and shaping rules; it is not the base. Every shared glyph is
225: transplanted from Manjari, and the donor is instantiated at the weight that
226: matches Manjari's pen.
227: 
228: The four families are deliberately separate variable fonts rather than one
229: merged font. Scripts have different GSUB/GPOS tables, glyph names, mark
230: attachments and win metrics; merging them would create conflicts in shared
231: Latin, punctuation and mark glyphs. Separate families also match how
232: Anek, Noto and most multiscript systems ship, and let each script keep its own
233: line height.
234: 
235: ### 9.2 Sources
236: 
237: | Branch | Base | Script donor | Upstream |
238: |---|---|---|---|
239: | Malayalam | Manjari | — | smc/fonts/manjari |
240: | Devanagari | Manjari | Noto Sans Devanagari VF | notofonts/devanagari |
241: | Tamil | Manjari | Noto Sans Tamil VF | notofonts/tamil |
242: | Telugu | Manjari | Noto Sans Telugu VF | notofonts/telugu |
243: | Kannada | Manjari | Noto Sans Kannada VF | notofonts/kannada |
244: 
245: The donor variable fonts are instantiated at the weight that matches
246: Manjari's stroke: `wght=360` for Regular and `wght=550` for Bold (Telugu uses
247: `340`/`500` because its base stem is heavier). They are then stripped of
248: hinting and variation tables and scaled to 1000 UPM (they are already 1000).
249: The Manjari base is scaled to 1000 UPM, stripped of hinting, and given the two
250: Latin case pairs (U+010F, U+01D1) that Manjari lacks. The vendored files and
251: SHA-256 checksums are in `sources/base/README.md` and
252: `sources/donors/README.md`.
253: 
254: ### 9.3 Script-specific aperture profiles
255: 
256: The warp is still point-preserving, but the profiles differ because the
257: scripts do not share one counter grammar.
258: 
259: | Script | hole_bump | peak_bump | freeze | sigma_f | Notes |
260: |---|---:|---:|---|---:|---|
261: | Devanagari | 110 | 60 | absolute y=545, fade 120 | 0.22 | Keeps the shirorekha straight; only loops below it open |
262: | Tamil | 100 | 25 | top 18% | 0.30 | Gentler; concentrated in the fewer closed loops |
263: | Telugu | 110 | 40 | none | 0.28 | Full loop warp |
264: | Kannada | 110 | 36 | none | 0.28 | Full loop warp |
265: 
266: `PETAL_WARP` now supports `only` (a glyph-name set), `freeze_top` (fraction),
267: `freeze_above` (absolute y), `freeze_fade`, `peak_max_frac`/`peak_max_y` and
268: `valley_bump`. With the defaults these are no-ops, which is why the Malayalam
269: build remains byte-identical.
270: 
271: The **absolute freeze** is the important Devanagari detail. Devanagari base
272: letters share a headline at roughly y=570–622; freezing above y=545 leaves the
273: headline and its junctions untouched, while the counter tops below 545 can
274: rise. A 120-unit fade avoids a hard step at the freeze boundary. The first
275: attempt used a per-glyph percentage freeze and a wide Gaussian, which pulled
276: the headline at the stem junctions; the absolute freeze plus a narrower
277: `sigma_f=0.22` fixed it.
278: 
279: ### 9.4 Glyph filtering
280: 
281: `tools/multiscript.py` first transplants every Manjari codepoint outside the
282: Malayalam block into the donor, using the donor's glyph name where one already
283: exists so the donor's GSUB/GPOS keeps working. Missing Manjari glyphs are
284: appended. Composites are flattened during the transplant, so a Manjari
285: composite cannot become a nested component inside a donor composite.
286: 
287: `petal_warp` then accepts `only`, a set of glyph names. The build computes that
288: set with `fontTools.subset`: it starts from the script's codepoints and closes
289: over GSUB, so conjuncts, half forms, reph forms, contextual variants and matras
290: are included. The Manjari shared set is subtracted, so Latin, punctuation and
291: digits stay in Manjari's style and are never warped.
292: 
293: The closure sizes (excluding `.notdef`) are 735 Devanagari, 166 Tamil, 723
294: Telugu and 414 Kannada glyphs.
295: 
296: `merge_latin_kerning` then appends Manjari's `latn` `kern` lookups to the
297: donor's GPOS and points the donor's `latn` language systems at the new
298: feature. The shared Latin therefore keeps Manjari's kerning as well as its
299: outlines and advances; the donor's script-specific GPOS is untouched.
300: 
301: ### 9.5 Metrics
302: 
303: The families use Manjari's typographic metrics (`sTypoAscender=800`,
304: `sTypoDescender=-300`, `sTypoLineGap=0`) so the shared Latin and the script
305: text sit on one line-height system. The win metrics are computed from the
306: actual outline extents, because the script donors have marks that reach above
307: and below Manjari's Latin:
308: 
309: ```
310: usWinAscent  = max(sTypoAscender, ceil(yMax) + 50)
311: usWinDescent = max(-sTypoDescender, ceil(-yMin) + 50)
312: ```
313: 
314: Devanagari's Vedic marks reach y=1347, so its win ascent is 1397; the typo
315: ascender stays at Manjari's 800, which means fontbakery reports the expected
316: `typoAscender` warning for the tall Manjari `Agrave` and Vedic marks. All
317: families set `USE_TYPO_METRICS`.
318: 
319: ### 9.6 Testing and QA
320: 
321: `tests/test_multiscript.py` checks, for all four scripts:
322: 
323: - `fvar` `APER=0…100`, default 100, and STAT values 0/50/100;
324: - the Manjari base and Noto donor copyright/designer credits in name IDs 0
325:   and 9, and the OFL notice in name ID 13;
326: - that `H`, `a`, `0`, `.` and the word space are byte-for-byte Manjari's
327:   outlines and advances in both Regular and Bold, and that the `AV`, `To`
328:   and `Wa` kern pairs match Manjari's;
329: - shaping of every case, display word and paragraph at APER 0/50/100, with
330:   identical glyph names and advances and no `.notdef`;
331: - full cmap coverage of the script donor, and shaping every script codepoint
332:   (marks with a base consonant);
333: - outline variation between APER 0 and 100, and a guard that Latin `H` is
334:   unchanged;
335: - static Round/Petal instances, names and the fact that they differ;
336: - COLRv1/CPAL structure in both Spectrum builds.
337: 
338: Fontbakery `check-universal` reports **0 FAIL** on all eight new Regular/Bold
339: VFs. The exclusions are the same as Malayalam:
340: 
341: - `opentype/fvar/regular_coords_correct` (custom `APER` axis);
342: - `alt_caron` (Czech/Slovak-specific);
343: - `opentype/fsselection` and `opentype/mac_style` for Bold (fontbakery infers
344:   "Regular" from the custom axis and cannot see the Bold style, although the
345:   OS/2 and `head` bits are correct).
346: 
347: The STAT value labels for the new families are `0`, `50`, `100` rather than
348: `Round`, `Bloom`, `Petal`: the family name plus the poetic label would exceed
349: Microsoft's 31-character family+style limit. The `fvar` named instances keep
350: the poetic names, and the specimen and documentation use them.
351: 
352: Inherited donor warnings (not introduced by this project) include:
353: 
354: - GDEF mark-class warnings for Vedic characters;
355: - a missing `avar` table (the APER axis is linear, so no mapping is needed);
356: - long Vedic glyph names and unreachable Vedic variants;
357: - a soft hyphen in the donor font;
358: - a `typoAscender` warning because Manjari's tall accented Latin and the
359:   Vedic marks extend above the 800-unit typo ascender. The win metrics are
360:   computed from the actual extents, so nothing clips.
361: 
362: These are recorded rather than silenced, because changing GDEF classes or
363: removing Vedic glyphs could break shaping.
364: 
365: ### 9.7 Multiscript limits
366: 
367: - Manjari contains no Devanagari, Tamil, Telugu or Kannada outlines. The
368:   script-specific letters therefore come from the Noto donors; only the
369:   shared glyphs and the design system are literally Manjari. A future release
370:   could draw those letters from Manjari's pen, but that is a new type-design
371:   project, not a build change.
372: - The donor's Latin GPOS mark features still use the donor's anchors with
373:   Manjari's Latin outlines. Precomposed accented letters are Manjari's own
374:   glyphs; decomposed mark sequences may need a small anchor pass.
375: - Tamil has fewer closed counters than the other scripts, so its APER change
376:   is deliberately subtler. A more radical Tamil cut would need new stroke
377:   terminals, not just a counter warp.
378: - The four families are separate fonts. A merged all-in-one font is not
379:   planned because of the shaping and glyph-name conflicts described above.
380: - The Spectrum gradient is the same font-unit range for every script; a
381:   per-script baseline calibration could be a future refinement.

1: # Kallar — design & engineering notes
2: 
3: ## 1. The idea
4: 
5: Malayalam is a loop script. The loop head (തല) is the script's most recognisable
6: gesture: a round counter, an opening, a tail. Most Malayalam typefaces treat
7: that loop as a circle or an oval. Kallar treats it as a **gateway**.
8: 
9: At `APER 0` the counter is the classic round loop inherited from Manjari. As
10: `APER` rises, the crown of the counter lifts into a soft point: the negative
11: space becomes a lotus petal / a temple doorway. The outer silhouette follows
12: with a gentler version of the same gesture, so open arches (മ, ന, ത) and closed
13: loops (ക, ഖ, ങ) share one rhythm. The result is not a decorative overlay; the
14: *counters themselves* change shape.
15: 
16: The second layer is colour. Sarvam's identity uses a blue → orange spectrum and
17: a lotus/gateway monogram. Kallar Spectrum carries a vertical
18: blue → orange gradient inside the font with COLRv1, clipped to each glyph. At
19: text sizes the tops are blue, the baseline zone is pink/orange and the
20: descenders are gold — one continuous field across the text block.
21: 
22: The family is deliberately a **display** companion, not a replacement for a
23: text face. It is designed to be set large, where the petal crowns and the
24: spectrum are visible.
25: 
26: ## 2. Why Manjari is the skeleton
27: 
28: The project's first two versions attempted a fully from-scratch parametric
29: Malayalam design (`legacy/`, `tools/glyphs_ml.py`). That work proved the
30: pipeline and the shaping stack, but matching the structural subtlety of a
31: production Malayalam face — the exact placement of loops, the counter rhythm,
32: the conjunct grammar — is a years-long project. For the production release we
33: made a deliberate choice:
34: 
35: - use **Manjari** (SIL OFL 1.1, by Santhosh Thottingal / SMC) as the
36:   structural foundation, because its loops and proportions are already a
37:   high-quality expression of the script;
38: - keep the base unmodified in `sources/base/` and record the transformation in
39:   code;
40: - do the new work where it is genuinely new: the aperture engine, the variable
41:   axis, the colour build, the metrics and the specimen.
42: 
43: This is a common and legitimate model in type design: a new face can share a
44: skeleton with an established one while having a distinct design language. The
45: derived font is renamed, the original copyright is preserved in the name table,
46: and the build is reproducible. The OFL permits this; the attribution is in the
47: font metadata, the README, the specimen and `AUTHORS.md`.
48: 
49: ## 3. The aperture transform
50: 
51: ### 3.1 Point compatibility
52: 
53: `varLib` requires masters with identical point topology. The transform
54: therefore only **moves existing TrueType points**; it never adds or removes
55: contours or points. Both the round master and the petal master start from the
56: same scaled Manjari source:
57: 
58: ```
59: Manjari-Regular.ttf (2048 UPM)
60:   └─ scale_upem → 1000 UPM
61:        ├─ round master: no warp
62:        └─ petal master: petal_warp()
63: ```
64: 
65: Because the point count, contour order and glyph order are unchanged, the
66: `gvar` deltas are exact and interpolation is smooth at every intermediate
67: value.
68: 
69: ### 3.2 Counter crowns
70: 
71: For each hole contour:
72: 
73: 1. compute its bbox and centre;
74: 2. for each point in the upper 55% of the hole, compute `u = (x-cx)/rx`,
75:    `v = (y-ymin)/h`, `t = (v-0.45)/0.55`;
76: 3. find the nearest outer-contour point with a KD-tree;
77: 4. lift the point by
78:    `bump * (1-u²) * t²`, where `bump = min(hole_bump, cap_frac * distance)`;
79: 5. pinch it horizontally by `pin * u * t²` to sharpen the crown.
80: 
81: The distance cap is essential. Manjari's strokes are ~65 units at 1000 UPM; an
82: uncapped 110-unit lift would push the counter through the outer contour and
83: create a hairline notch. Capping at 55% of the nearest stroke thickness makes
84: the petal safe on every glyph, including the tiny loops of ഇ, ഈ, ഠ and the
85: historical numerals. The cap varies per point, so the warp stays smooth.
86: 
87: ### 3.3 Outer crowns
88: 
89: Open counters (മ, ന, ത, യ, …) are not holes; their inner edge is part of the
90: outer contour. To bring them into the same language, the engine finds local
91: maxima on every outer contour in the upper half of the glyph and applies a
92: smooth Gaussian lift:
93: 
94: ```
95: wy = clamp((y - (gymin+0.35*gh)) / (0.65*gh), 0, 1)
96: pull = exp(-((x-px)/sigma)^2) * wy^2
97: y += peak_bump * pull
98: x -= 0.5 * pinch * (x-px) * exp(...) * wy
99: ```
100: 
101: `sigma` is relative to the contour width, so wide letters get a broad crown and
102: narrow letters a tighter one. The lift is subtle enough that the counters stay
103: open and readable.
104: 
105: ### 3.4 Parameters at 1000 UPM
106: 
107: | parameter | value | role |
108: |---|---:|---|
109: | `hole_bump` | 110 | maximum counter crown lift |
110: | `peak_bump` | 40 | outer crown lift |
111: | `sigma_f` | 0.28 | crown width relative to contour width |
112: | `pinch` | 0.055 | horizontal sharpening |
113: | `cap_frac` | 0.55 | maximum lift as a fraction of local stroke |
114: 
115: The static `APER 0`, `50`, `100` instances are produced with
116: `fontTools.varLib.instancer`.
117: 
118: ## 4. Metrics
119: 
120: The base is scaled to 1000 UPM. The final metrics are:
121: 
122: - `sTypoAscender = 800`, `sTypoDescender = -300`, `sTypoLineGap = 0`
123: - `hhea.ascent = 800`, `hhea.descent = -300`, `lineGap = 0`
124: - `usWinAscent = 1100`, `usWinDescent = 700` (the real glyph extents are
125:   roughly -614…1075, so the win metrics never clip)
126: - `USE_TYPO_METRICS` (OS/2 fsSelection bit 7) is set.
127: - The vertical metrics are intentionally generous: Malayalam marks, chillus
128:   and the Latin superscripts extend above the nominal ascender.
129: 
130: Manjari's advances, kerning and GSUB/GPOS are preserved. The warp only changes
131: outline coordinates, so spacing and shaping stay stable across the axis.
132: 
133: ## 5. COLRv1 spectrum
134: 
135: The Spectrum builds start from the variable Regular and Bold and add:
136: 
137: - `CPAL` with a 7-entry palette:
138:   `#181E5C`, `#2B3FB0`, `#5C64DB`, `#A06CD2`, `#D973A0`, `#EE7944`, `#F9C36D`.
139: - `COLR` version 1 with one `BaseGlyphPaintRecord` per non-empty glyph:
140:   `PaintGlyph(glyph)` → `PaintLinearGradient`.
141: - The gradient runs from `(0, 620)` to `(0, -120)`, with the rotation point
142:   `(500, 620)` (perpendicular to the gradient direction). The gradient is in
143:   font units and is clipped by the glyph outline. This range puts blue at the
144:   top of the body, orange near the baseline and gold in the descenders.
145: - 907 glyphs carry a paint record in the Bold build and 913 in the Regular
146:   build; the rest fall back to monochrome.
147: 
148: Browsers/apps with COLRv1 (Chrome, Edge, Figma, recent Safari) paint the
149: gradient; apps without it render the base outlines. The specimen also shows a
150: CSS gradient-clipped version so the visual idea is visible everywhere.
151: 
152: ## 6. Testing
153: 
154: `tests/test_kallar.py` checks:
155: 
156: - `fvar` axis `APER = 0…100`, default 100;
157: - `STAT` axis values Round / Bloom / Petal;
158: - the OFL name table and Manjari attribution on every build;
159: - shaping of 35+ Malayalam strings at `APER 0`, `50`, `100`, with identical
160:   glyph sequences;
161: - coverage of every assigned Malayalam codepoint;
162: - outline variation between the extremes;
163: - COLR/CPAL structure, 907 paint records and 7 palette entries.
164: 
165: The HTML specimen was also checked in headless Chromium 156: the embedded
166: variable fonts load, the APER slider changes the live instance, and the
167: `Kallar Spectrum` sample paints its COLRv1 gradient in the browser.
168: 
169: Builds are reproducible: `head.created`/`head.modified` are pinned to a fixed
170: date and `recalcTimestamp` is disabled, so repeated `make kallar` runs produce
171: byte-identical TTF and WOFF2 files. `make proofs` is deterministic too.
172: 
173: The old `tests/test_font.py` still covers the legacy draft.
174: 
175: ## 7. Fontbakery notes
176: 
177: The Regular font passes `fontbakery check-universal` with two exclusions that
178: do not apply to this design:
179: 
180: - `opentype/fvar/regular_coords_correct` assumes a registered `wght`/`wdth`
181:   axis; Kallar's only axis is the custom `APER`.
182: - `alt_caron` is a Czech/Slovak-specific check that wants `ď` to use a
183:   non-standard caron glyph. The Latin `ď` here uses a combining caron, which
184:   is typographically correct; the check is not relevant to a Malayalam face.
185: 
186: For the Bold and Spectrum builds, `opentype/fsselection` and
187: `opentype/mac_style` also need excluding because fontbakery infers "Bold"
188: from a `wght` axis or a filename convention and cannot see the custom-axis
189: Bold style; the OS/2 and `head` values themselves are correct. Run the QA
190: target with:
191: 
192: ```bash
193: make qa
194: ```
195: 
196: The specimen HTML and COLRv1 paint were verified in headless Chromium 156.
197: 
198: ## 8. Known limits / next work
199: 
200: - The transform is derived from Manjari's skeleton; it is not a new
201:   construction from a blank page. A future release could redraw the skeleton
202:   from the same aperture grammar while keeping the axis.
203: - The Spectrum gradient is static; a `COLRv1` variable gradient tied to `APER`
204:   would be the next step.
205: - A `wght` axis would need point-compatible masters from a variable source
206:   (Noto Sans Malayalam is a candidate) or a carefully offset master.
207: - The display cut is optimised for large sizes. A text-optimised cut with
208:   smaller petal lifts and looser spacing is planned.
209: 
210: ## 9. The multiscript extension
211: 
212: ### 9.1 Manjari is the base of every family
213: 
214: The original idea is preserved: all five Kallar families start from the
215: **Manjari** skeleton. Manjari supplies the shared Latin, digits, punctuation,
216: symbols, spacing, metrics and design language. The Malayalam family is Manjari
217: throughout.
218: 
219: Manjari is a Malayalam + Latin face, so it has no Devanagari, Tamil, Telugu or
220: Kannada glyphs. Drawing four new scripts from a blank page would be a
221: years-long design project, and a from-scratch skeleton would not have Manjari's
222: quality. The release therefore uses one OFL **script donor** per
223: non-Malayalam script. The donor supplies only the script-specific letter
224: structures and shaping rules; it is not the base. Every shared glyph is
225: transplanted from Manjari, and the donor is instantiated at the weight that
226: matches Manjari's pen.
227: 
228: The four families are deliberately separate variable fonts rather than one
229: merged font. Scripts have different GSUB/GPOS tables, glyph names, mark
230: attachments and win metrics; merging them would create conflicts in shared
231: Latin, punctuation and mark glyphs. Separate families also match how
232: Anek, Noto and most multiscript systems ship, and let each script keep its own
233: line height.
234: 
235: ### 9.2 Sources
236: 
237: | Branch | Base | Script donor | Upstream |
238: |---|---|---|---|
239: | Malayalam | Manjari | — | smc/fonts/manjari |
240: | Devanagari | Manjari | Noto Sans Devanagari VF | notofonts/devanagari |
241: | Tamil | Manjari | Noto Sans Tamil VF | notofonts/tamil |
242: | Telugu | Manjari | Noto Sans Telugu VF | notofonts/telugu |
243: | Kannada | Manjari | Noto Sans Kannada VF | notofonts/kannada |
244: 
245: The donor variable fonts are instantiated at the weight that matches
246: Manjari's stroke: `wght=360` for Regular and `wght=550` for Bold (Telugu uses
247: `340`/`500` because its base stem is heavier). They are then stripped of
248: hinting and variation tables and scaled to 1000 UPM (they are already 1000).
249: The Manjari base is scaled to 1000 UPM, stripped of hinting, and given the two
250: Latin case pairs (U+010F, U+01D1) that Manjari lacks. The vendored files and
251: SHA-256 checksums are in `sources/base/README.md` and
252: `sources/donors/README.md`.
253: 
254: ### 9.3 Script-specific aperture profiles
255: 
256: The warp is still point-preserving, but the profiles differ because the
257: scripts do not share one counter grammar.
258: 
259: | Script | hole_bump | peak_bump | freeze | sigma_f | Notes |
260: |---|---:|---:|---|---:|---|
261: | Devanagari | 110 | 60 | absolute y=545, fade 120 | 0.22 | Keeps the shirorekha straight; only loops below it open |
262: | Tamil | 100 | 25 | top 18% | 0.30 | Gentler; concentrated in the fewer closed loops |
263: | Telugu | 110 | 40 | none | 0.28 | Full loop warp |
264: | Kannada | 110 | 36 | none | 0.28 | Full loop warp |
265: 
266: `PETAL_WARP` now supports `only` (a glyph-name set), `freeze_top` (fraction),
267: `freeze_above` (absolute y), `freeze_fade`, `peak_max_frac`/`peak_max_y` and
268: `valley_bump`. With the defaults these are no-ops, which is why the Malayalam
269: build remains byte-identical.
270: 
271: The **absolute freeze** is the important Devanagari detail. Devanagari base
272: letters share a headline at roughly y=570–622; freezing above y=545 leaves the
273: headline and its junctions untouched, while the counter tops below 545 can
274: rise. A 120-unit fade avoids a hard step at the freeze boundary. The first
275: attempt used a per-glyph percentage freeze and a wide Gaussian, which pulled
276: the headline at the stem junctions; the absolute freeze plus a narrower
277: `sigma_f=0.22` fixed it.
278: 
279: ### 9.4 Glyph filtering
280: 
281: `tools/multiscript.py` first transplants every Manjari codepoint outside the
282: Malayalam block into the donor, using the donor's glyph name where one already
283: exists so the donor's GSUB/GPOS keeps working. Missing Manjari glyphs are
284: appended. Composites are flattened during the transplant, so a Manjari
285: composite cannot become a nested component inside a donor composite.
286: 
287: `petal_warp` then accepts `only`, a set of glyph names. The build computes that
288: set with `fontTools.subset`: it starts from the script's codepoints and closes
289: over GSUB, so conjuncts, half forms, reph forms, contextual variants and matras
290: are included. The Manjari shared set is subtracted, so Latin, punctuation and
291: digits stay in Manjari's style and are never warped.
292: 
293: The closure sizes (excluding `.notdef`) are 735 Devanagari, 166 Tamil, 723
294: Telugu and 414 Kannada glyphs.
295: 
296: `merge_latin_kerning` then appends Manjari's `latn` `kern` lookups to the
297: donor's GPOS and points the donor's `latn` language systems at the new
298: feature. The shared Latin therefore keeps Manjari's kerning as well as its
299: outlines and advances; the donor's script-specific GPOS is untouched.
300: 
301: ### 9.5 Metrics
302: 
303: The families use Manjari's typographic metrics (`sTypoAscender=800`,
304: `sTypoDescender=-300`, `sTypoLineGap=0`) so the shared Latin and the script
305: text sit on one line-height system. The win metrics are computed from the
306: actual outline extents, because the script donors have marks that reach above
307: and below Manjari's Latin:
308: 
309: ```
310: usWinAscent  = max(sTypoAscender, ceil(yMax) + 50)
311: usWinDescent = max(-sTypoDescender, ceil(-yMin) + 50)
312: ```
313: 
314: Devanagari's Vedic marks reach y=1347, so its win ascent is 1397; the typo
315: ascender stays at Manjari's 800, which means fontbakery reports the expected
316: `typoAscender` warning for the tall Manjari `Agrave` and Vedic marks. All
317: families set `USE_TYPO_METRICS`.
318: 
319: ### 9.6 Testing and QA
320: 
321: `tests/test_multiscript.py` checks, for all four scripts:
322: 
323: - `fvar` `APER=0…100`, default 100, and STAT values 0/50/100;
324: - the Manjari base and Noto donor copyright/designer credits in name IDs 0
325:   and 9, and the OFL notice in name ID 13;
326: - that `H`, `a`, `0`, `.` and the word space are byte-for-byte Manjari's
327:   outlines and advances in both Regular and Bold, and that the `AV`, `To`
328:   and `Wa` kern pairs match Manjari's;
329: - shaping of every case, display word and paragraph at APER 0/50/100, with
330:   identical glyph names and advances and no `.notdef`;
331: - full cmap coverage of the script donor, and shaping every script codepoint
332:   (marks with a base consonant);
333: - outline variation between APER 0 and 100, and a guard that Latin `H` is
334:   unchanged;
335: - static Round/Petal instances, names and the fact that they differ;
336: - COLRv1/CPAL structure in both Spectrum builds.
337: 
338: Fontbakery `check-universal` reports **0 FAIL** on all eight new Regular/Bold
339: VFs. The exclusions are the same as Malayalam:
340: 
341: - `opentype/fvar/regular_coords_correct` (custom `APER` axis);
342: - `alt_caron` (Czech/Slovak-specific);
343: - `opentype/fsselection` and `opentype/mac_style` for Bold (fontbakery infers
344:   "Regular" from the custom axis and cannot see the Bold style, although the
345:   OS/2 and `head` bits are correct).
346: 
347: The STAT value labels for the new families are `0`, `50`, `100` rather than
348: `Round`, `Bloom`, `Petal`: the family name plus the poetic label would exceed
349: Microsoft's 31-character family+style limit. The `fvar` named instances keep
350: the poetic names, and the specimen and documentation use them.
351: 
352: Inherited donor warnings (not introduced by this project) include:
353: 
354: - GDEF mark-class warnings for Vedic characters;
355: - a missing `avar` table (the APER axis is linear, so no mapping is needed);
356: - long Vedic glyph names and unreachable Vedic variants;
357: - a soft hyphen in the donor font;
358: - a `typoAscender` warning because Manjari's tall accented Latin and the
359:   Vedic marks extend above the 800-unit typo ascender. The win metrics are
360:   computed from the actual extents, so nothing clips.
361: 
362: These are recorded rather than silenced, because changing GDEF classes or
363: removing Vedic glyphs could break shaping.
364: 
365: ### 9.7 Multiscript limits
366: 
367: - Manjari contains no Devanagari, Tamil, Telugu or Kannada outlines. The
368:   script-specific letters therefore come from the Noto donors; only the
369:   shared glyphs and the design system are literally Manjari. A future release
370:   could draw those letters from Manjari's pen, but that is a new type-design
371:   project, not a build change.
372: - The donor's Latin GPOS mark features still use the donor's anchors with
373:   Manjari's Latin outlines. Precomposed accented letters are Manjari's own
374:   glyphs; decomposed mark sequences may need a small anchor pass.
375: - Tamil has fewer closed counters than the other scripts, so its APER change
376:   is deliberately subtler. A more radical Tamil cut would need new stroke
377:   terminals, not just a counter warp.
378: - The four families are separate fonts. A merged all-in-one font is not
379:   planned because of the shaping and glyph-name conflicts described above.
380: - The Spectrum gradient is the same font-unit range for every script; a
381:   per-script baseline calibration could be a future refinement.

Now I need to decide scope with user. User said: "Remove all legacy and unnecessary things from this project. Like old font specimens, mention of the version history etc."

Likely expectations:
1. Delete legacy/ directory, legacy sources, legacy tools, legacy config, legacy test.
2. Delete old working proof images (ref_*, tune_*, ab_*, iter*, ezh_*, plus unused kallar_hero.png, kallar_spectrum.png).
3. Remove version history section and legacy mentions from README, AUTHORS, NOTES, FONTLOG.
4. Possibly delete FONTLOG.txt entirely since it's version history? Hmm. FONTLOG is standard for OFL fonts and includes license/attribution. But user explicitly says "mention of version history" — likely the README "Version history" section, not necessarily FONTLOG. However FONTLOG is *literally* version history. I need to decide.

Let me check git to see tracked files. Maybe the cleanest is to remove FONTLOG.txt entirely and any references. But OFL best practice recommends FONTLOG. Yet user asks remove unnecessary things. Hmm. The safest interpretation: remove legacy and version-history mentions from docs, but keep FONTLOG? Actually if I keep FONTLOG with v0.1/v0.2/Ezhuthu entries, I haven't removed version history mentions. The user explicitly wants "mention of the version history etc." removed. So I should delete FONTLOG.txt or rewrite it to a minimal changelog without legacy. But then fonts' name table may reference FONTLOG? Let's check kallar.py and multiscript.py. Search "FONTLOG".

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Kallar — the aperture-variable Malayalam display family.

Design idea
-----------
Every Malayalam loop/arch is treated as a *gateway*: a round base that rises
to a soft lotus-petal crown.  The transformation is parametric and applied to
a proven open-source Malayalam skeleton (Manjari by Santhosh Thottingal /
SMC, OFL-1.1).  It is exposed as the ``APER`` (Aperture) variation axis:

    APER 0    classic round Manjari-derived forms
    APER 100  the full petal / gateway display cut (default)

The same outlines are then given a COLRv1 blue→orange spectrum in the
``Kallar Spectrum`` build, referencing Sarvam's visual language
without copying its wordmark.

All masters are point-compatible: the warp only moves existing TrueType
points, so varLib can interpolate between them cleanly.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import copy
import math
import os
import sys

from fontTools.designspaceLib import (
    AxisDescriptor,
    DesignSpaceDocument,
    InstanceDescriptor,
    SourceDescriptor,
)
from fontTools.ttLib import TTFont
from fontTools.ttLib.scaleUpem import scale_upem
from fontTools.varLib import build as varlib_build
from fontTools.varLib.instancer import instantiateVariableFont
from fontTools.colorLib.builder import buildCOLR, buildCPAL
from fontTools.ttLib.tables import otTables as ot
====
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Kallar multiscript — Manjari is the base of every family.

The whole Kallar system starts from the same **Manjari** skeleton.  Manjari
supplies the shared Latin, digits, punctuation, symbols, spacing, metrics and
design language of every family.  The Malayalam family is Manjari throughout.

Manjari is a Malayalam + Latin face, so it has no Devanagari, Tamil, Telugu or
Kannada outlines.  Those four families therefore use the corresponding Noto
Sans faces as **script donors**: the donor supplies only the script-specific
letter structures (and the GSUB/GPOS rules that shape them), while every
shared glyph is transplanted from Manjari.  The donor is instantiated at the
weight that matches Manjari's pen, so the script letters sit at the same
stroke weight as the Manjari base.

Each family is a separate variable font because the scripts have different
shaping tables, glyph sets and vertical metrics.  They share the APER axis
(0..100, default 100), the five named stops, the Spectrum palette and the
static Round/Petal instances, so they can be used together as one type system.

Usage:
    python tools/multiscript.py                 # all four scripts
    python tools/multiscript.py devanagari      # one script
    python tools/multiscript.py tamil telugu    # a subset

The build is deterministic: the base fonts are vendored, the timestamps are
pinned and the transform only moves existing TrueType points, so repeated runs
produce byte-identical files.
"""
from __future__ import annotations
====
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Ezhuthu font builder.

Pipeline: parametric glyph designs (glyphs_ml) -> MalayalamFont (ufoLib2 subclass,
vendored from SMC Nupuram) with GSUB/GPOS via fontFeatures -> UFO -> ufo2ft
compilers -> TTF / OTF / WOFF2.
"""
import os
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))

import yaml
from munch import munchify
from ufoLib2.objects import Anchor, Component, Glyph

from glyphs_ml import DESIGNS, build_ml
import shapes
from malayalamfont import MalayalamFont
from shapes import GlyphBuilder

## Building from source

The build is Python + fontTools + varLib + COLRv1.

```bash
make venv            # create .venv and install dependencies
make kallar          # Malayalam: masters, variable fonts, Spectrum, instances
make multiscript     # Devanagari, Tamil, Telugu and Kannada families
make test            # shaping, variation and colour tests for all five scripts
make proofs          # specimen PNGs, GIF and both interactive HTML specimens
make pdf             # Malayalam vector PDF specimen
make pdf-multiscript # multiscript vector PDF specimen
make qa              # fontbakery on Malayalam Regular and Bold
make qa-multiscript  # fontbakery on the four new Regular/Bold families
```

### Source layout

| Path | What it is |
|---|---|
| `tools/kallar.py` | The aperture engine, Malayalam build, spectrum, instances |
| `tools/multiscript.py` | The Manjari-base Devanagari/Tamil/Telugu/Kannada build driver |
| `tools/specimen.py` | Malayalam proof images and brand mockups |
| `tools/specimen_multiscript.py` | Multiscript hero, axis and script sheets |
| `tools/specimen_html.py` | Self-contained Malayalam HTML specimen |
| `tools/specimen_multiscript_html.py` | Self-contained multiscript HTML specimen |
| `tools/pdf.py` | Chromium PDF printer |
| `sources/base/` | Manjari base fonts + upstream OFL text |
| `sources/donors/` | Noto Sans script donors + upstream OFL texts |
| `tests/test_kallar.py` | Malayalam shaping, variation and colour tests |
| `tests/test_multiscript.py` | Multiscript axes, Manjari base, metadata, coverage and colour tests |

### Reproducible builds

`head.created` and `head.modified` are pinned to a fixed date and
`recalcTimestamp` is disabled. Repeated `make kallar` and `make multiscript`
runs produce byte-identical TTF and WOFF2 files. `make proofs` is
deterministic too.

---

---TAIL---
|---|---|
| Malayalam | Full hole-and-crown warp; the original Kallar cut |
| Devanagari | Counters-only below an absolute headline freeze |
| Tamil | Gentler profile concentrated in the fewer closed loops |
| Telugu | Full hole-and-crown warp |
| Kannada | Full hole-and-crown warp |
